Um dos filmes mais repugnantes que eu já vi na minha vida. Os primeiros cinquenta minutos contém o humor mais insuportável possível para um filme que aborda a segunda guerra mundial. Roberto Benigni é completamente azucrinante; "olha só como eu sou engraçado! Eu falo rápido demais, chamo a mulher de princesa o tempo todo e sou um plágio horrível de Charles Chaplin!" Até tem umas duas ou três cenas interessantes, e por causa delas, evita que o filme seja nota zero. De resto, absurdamente intolerável; cada personagem, cada fala, cada situação deplorável, tudo é irritante. E pra piorar, no final, chegam os soldados estadunidenses, e o pequeno Josué comemora como se os vingadores tivessem salvado o mundo. Vai se foder.

For the first time in a while I genuinely hated a film I watched and was forced to continue it. This was said to be a ‘Romantic Dark Comedy with Drama’ yet it felt more like just shitty comedy with some love interest and tasteless drama. An Italian film by apparently the ‘Italian Robin Williams’ though it couldn’t be more from that at all. It begins with comedy and immediately makes a woman the chase prize. Constantly butting in and following her around eventually sexually harassing her in front of her own house. The main protagonist chases this woman around then realizes she has a husband and is soon to be married but needs to be saved (so damn original). The father has him running the book store within the first 10 minutes of his reveal and he throws tantrums when he has to take a damn shower. By no surprise the Nazis come and take both Joshua and the main character. Loaded up into a train and the wife follows suit. If there was any chance of making someone feel fear for their now horrible position. It was immediately lost when he runs in search for his wife in front of ‘SS’ soldiers with loaded guns and they dont kill him. I knew from this moment this immediately put the film into the trashcan for me. This not only happens once but at least five to six times throughout the film where there was zero tension or repercussions for ones actions in a ‘ CONCENTRATION CAMP’ The main character continues to joke entirely throughout the film even during hard labor scenes and is never shot and killed for it. It almost as if it’s a parody of the Nazi camps more than trying to show symbolism of Jewish suffering. He convinces the child this is all a game to win a tank and that its a Halo game of ‘King of the Hill.’ The other children are killed off screen by gas chamber and so with the older adults. During the main characters check up he is marked for death by gas chamber but ultimately. A Nazi doctor saves the main character from death… Yeah okay buddy and to add to that remark there is no inspections of their dorms allowing the child to remain COMPLETELY CLEAN and unharmed entirely. Joshua and protagonist continue to literally speak so loudly inside dorms and even outside and somehow never alert Nazis during their plans. This is what fucking amazed me genuinely how this was supposed to be ‘romantic.’ They find a literal radio for the Nazi camp and USE it to contact his wife / his mom. Screaming, yelling and laughing on this thing and despite this place crawling with soldiers both of them remained unharmed. Eventually in some way the Americans begin to raid this camp after like four days and they are ‘saved.’ Well almost but thats because the protagonist couldn’t wait to find his wife and was able to freely run around the camp. He ends up dying off screen (finally)  leaving the child inside an electrical box. The child leaves after everything has calmed down and is picked up by an American soldier and delivered to his mom. BOTH literally dont even care about what happened to their husband / father btw. Then the film ends… By far this is my most disliked film so far in my class / possibly my life this shit stinks.

ON A PILGRIMAGE THROUGH THE SILVER SCREEN, CHASING THE HIGHEST-RATED STARS OF LETTERBOXD How is it possible for us to dance upon the ashes, when the very ground we stand on is still wet with tears and congealed blood? I stand at the crossroads of guilt and anger, staring at a stage built by ego. There, one of humanity’s greatest tragedies—an industrial genocide that claimed millions of lives—is forcibly downsized, infantilized for the sake of a melodramatic reinforcement that feels so bizarre and cheap. They whisper, "Smile in the face of horror, and you will get through it." They chant a mantra, "Let everything happen to you, for no feeling is final." Yet to me, this is not beauty. This is a fascism of sentimentality, a cynical falsehood that wraps a gaping wound in colorful ribbons. I believe that humor can grow in any soil, even against the darkest backdrop, provided it is clever, sharp, and knows exactly where its target lies. But here, beneath the shadows of the cardboard castles they call concentration camps, the joke loses its soul. All that remains is overacting, clumsy antics fumbling in the dark, and an egoistic longing for the audience to fall in love with the protagonist. The first half of this film passes like an ordinary, unfunny sketch, filled with forced and foolish coincidences. But when the train carries them to the gates of hell, that is the exact moment my soul refuses to participate. They want us to be moved by the lie of a father who turns genocide into a game of hide-and-seek for his child. They want us to celebrate that falsehood as a sublime love. Yet, how can we turn our faces away from the honest truth? The Holocaust is not the backdrop for a cute slapstick joke. A concentration camp is not a playground where a child can whine to go home, only to be easily convinced to stay for the prize of a toy tank. If this film were honest for even a single second about that institutionalized cruelty—about the corpses rotting in the corner of one's eye, about the merciless executions over trivial matters—then this sweet illusion would shatter into pieces. Hiding the horror from our sight might be a visual technique, but hiding it from the reality of the characters is an insult to those who actually lived and died inside those gas chambers. To say that lying is the key to seeing that life is beautiful, or that looking away is the way to assimilate tragedy, is the most vulgar philosophy I have ever encountered. I cannot find it in my heart to be moved by this false happy ending. Perhaps people will think I am stone-hearted. But to me, allowing the Holocaust to be mixed with saccharine jokes is the true form of numbness. In the end, I can only slap my forehead in deep sorrow, realizing how cheap grief becomes when it is forced to smile just to satisfy a thirst for sentimental tears.

Eu fico imaginando Joseph Goebbels sentado numa sala de cinema escura e chorando de emoção ao perceber que nem o Ministério da Propaganda nazista conseguiu criar uma campanha tão eficiente para suavizar o Holocausto quanto A Vida é Bela. É exatamente isso que essa obra é, uma esquete que poderia ter sido encomendada pelo próprio Terceiro Reich para provar ao mundo que os campos de concentração não passavam de um grande parque de diversões, um acampamento de férias onde a maior ameaça era perder pontos numa gincana idiota. A câmera ofende a nossa inteligência a cada frame, chamando o espectador de burro na cara dura enquanto transforma a tragédia mais sombria da humanidade numa palhaçada histérica. Assistir a esse filme é pagar o ingresso mais caro do mundo para sentar na primeira fileira de um circo montado em cima de uma vala comum. O diretor veste o uniforme listrado do campo de extermínio com a mesma energia de um animador de festa infantil que errou o endereço e foi parar no nono círculo do Inferno de Dante. Ele contempla o fogo eterno consumindo a carne humana e decide que a melhor solução é fazer BICHINHOS DE BALÃO com as TRIPAS DOS CONDENADOS. A obra funciona como uma comédia macabra de situação, uma propaganda de limpeza higiênica capaz de fazer os arquitetos da Alemanha nazista chorarem de emoção ao perceberem o cinema lavando o sangue das câmaras de gás com sabonete de morango. Nós mergulhamos num delírio coletivo onde o genocídio mais brutal da história ganha uma paleta de cores adocicada e uma névoa branca de conto de fadas criada exclusivamente para blindar o estômago covarde da plateia. O protagonista Guido assume a forma do Flautista de Hamelin soprando uma melodia alucinógena de psicose pura. Ele arrasta a própria sanidade para o abismo e obriga o filho a sorrir enquanto o oxigênio do mundo acaba. A cena absurda do banquete italiano engarrafa o cinismo do projeto inteiro numa única imagem bizarra. O garçom equilibra um cachorro vivo numa bandeja de luxo e pergunta aos convidados se existe algo de errado com a presença dele ali. A metalinguagem acidental grita na nossa cara, o diretor serve uma anomalia grotesca em pratos de prata, exibe os dentes sujos de mentira e exige aplausos pela genialidade da sua pataquada. A postura corporal esquizofrênica do pai se mantém intacta até nos raros momentos de solidão, escancarando a falência moral de um roteiro absolutamente incapaz de encarar a morte de frente. A palhaçada ininterrupta sepulta qualquer traço de decência. A humilhação intelectual atinge o ápice da náusea no instante em que o portão de ferro do campo se abre, aqui o peso fantasmagórico de milhões de cadáveres transformados em fumaça exigia o silêncio mais esmagador que o audiovisual poderia registrar. A resposta da direção para o luto da humanidade é enfiar um tanque blindado rasgando a tela sob a marcha patriótica mais histérica e plástica do planeta. O veículo militar americano surge no cemitério com a sutileza de um trio elétrico atropelando os familiares de um velório, a libertação vira um comercial brilhante de margarina com a criança abraçando a mãe num festival de patriotismo barato e fogos de artifício. Roberto Benigni arquitetou o maior parque temático da culpa ocidental, um lugar obsceno onde o público dá um passeio de carrossel pelas cinzas do holocausto e sai pela loja de lembrancinhas comprando um chaveiro de esperança para chorar lágrimas purificadas de pura hipocrisia.

I will not contribute to this film’s ridiculous Letterboxd score any longer.  No, it isn’t truly a half star movie; it’s fine from a filmmaking perspective and some of the supporting performances are also fine, but Roberto Benigni remains an unfunny clown now just like he was then and this movie remains one of the most overrated and misguided major award winners of all time and  I think anyone who gives this one 5 stars is either too naive or too overcome by saccharine emotional manipulation to see what an absolute dog it is. My core problem with the film comes down to construction and concept where Nazi camps are whitewashed to be survivable in order for the games being played by Guido to work. The Holocaust becomes a backdrop that makes his whimsy look heroic, so the atrocity gets sanitized to serve the sentimentality; it’s Holocaust cinema for the Angel Studios crowd. The second half runs on a fantasy of what parental love can accomplish in a death camp, and the film never earns it because it never looks at what it's asking us to look away from. Benigni's mugging doesn't help. Compare Son of Saul, or even Schindler's List at its most manipulative, where, at least, the machinery and the monsters running it are shown. I also still hate the Italian clown climbing over the seats at the Oscars like a drunk idiot.  Fuck Roberto Benigni and his stupid antics and fuck this movie.  Insufferable tripe.  Watch Schindler’s List or The Pianist instead where reality and pain are at least portrayed visually and honestly. The Holocaust is no place for whimsy or jokes and it definitely isn’t a place where atrocities should be ignored for some temporary relief that was never granted in reality.

Das ist ja mal ein richtig radikaler Ansatz. Ein Film über den Holocaust, der sich als sentimentale Melodrama-Komödie (natürlich mit viel Kitsch) probiert. Ein jüdischer Vater innerhalb eines Konzentrationslagers überzeugt seinen kleinen Sohn davon das alles wäre nur ein Spiel, um ihn zu schützen. Hört sich zunächst vielleicht nach einer interessanten Idee an, ist aber doch ein ziemlich alberner Ansatz. Ja, auch Menschen in den dunkelsten Situationen nutzen Humor um sich am Leben zu erhalten. Das geht aber nur bis zu einem bestimmten Maß. Was das Drehbuch uns hier erzählt wäre in einem echten Konzentrationslager komplett unmöglich. Den Holocaust als Geschichte eines letztlich unzerstörlich hoffnungsvollen Menschen zu verfilmen, der mit Fantasie und Humor es schließlich erfolgreich schafft die Unschuld seines Sohnes innerhalb eines KZs zu bewahren, grenzt wirklich an einer historischen Realitätsverweigerung. Das Sterben zu dieser Zeit war absolut sinnlos. Die einzige wichtige Person, die hier stirbt, tut es um die eigene Familie zu retten. Dieser Tod hat einen Sinn. Sollte die Sinnlosigkeit und das absolute Scheitern nicht Thema eines Films über die Shoah sein? Hier haben wir stattdessen einen heroischen Tod und den Triumph der Unschuld und der Liebe. Ein volkommen missgeleiteter Ansatz auf den nur ein Comedian kommen kann. Vielleicht hat Harvey Weinstein, als er den Film in der wohl dreistesten Oscar-Kampagne jemals vermarktet hat, besser als alle Kritiker verstanden worum es sich hier handelt. Ein Produkt für die Massen, das bei allen Emotionen vorlockt und dennoch hoffnungsvoll und leicht zu verdauen bleibt. Mit einer sinnvollen Auseinandersetzung mit der Shoah hat das gar nichts zu tun.

Se avessi 0 conoscenze riguardo alle atrocità commesse verso gli ebrei durante gli anni della seconda guerra mondiale, Benigni mi avrebbe reso fascista. Per fortuna riesco a capire che questa è pura sbobba propagandistica verso l’america a cui “roberto!” ha succhiato il cazzo per togliere l’oscar ad Edward Norton.  Per quanto mi riguarda è un film terribile, cominciando dalla suddivisione in due parti: nella prima ci vengono presentati alcuni temi del film, facendoci credere che siano quelli su cui poi procederà tutta la narrazione, ma ad una certa c’è uno smorzamento e si finisce nel campo dì concentramento. E quando uno si aspetta un cambio totale di tono, ecco che tutto è visto dagli occhi del bambino e diventa un gioco. Questo film non è un’accusa al nazi-fascismo, ma una favola in cui il male non ha spiegazione e non si può prendere sul serio, andando a ironizzare su atti di crudeltà, ma non portando leggerezza sull’argomento, quanto semplicemente rendendo il tutto una parodia. Il bene, invece, arriva dal nulla e, seppure sia fondamentale nella storia, non funge da simbolo di speranza ma è solo un elemento propagandistico, che insieme ai vari elementi inseriti solo per commuovere lo spettatore, fa pensare che questo film sia davvero solo stato creato per un oscar. Il bambino non capisce cos’è successo per colpa del gioco, e ciò è sbagliatissimo. I bambini, in primis, devono imparare da subito cos’è successo in quel periodo perché sennò si finisce in una società in cui il fascismo e il nazismo esistono ancora e si diffondono specialmente tra i giovani. Naturalmente il tutto va portato a loro con leggerezza finché non raggiungano un’età adatta ad affrontare bene il tema, ma MAI bisogna far credere che sia stato tutto solo un gioco. Benigni mi ha davvero deluso.  Menomale che alla fine stira.

​A premissa de cruzar o horror de um centro de extermínio com a farsa do pastelão carrega um risco moral evidente. Na década de 1970, Jerry Lewis tentou algo na mesma linha em O Dia em que o Palhaço Chorou , interpretando um artista de circo que guiava crianças para as câmaras de gás. O resultado foi uma obra tida como tão deslocada em sua comédia e em seu sentimentalismo que (felizmente) acabou trancada em um cofre, julgada imprópria para exibição. Duas décadas mais tarde, Roberto Benigni recorreu à mesma fórmula em A Vida É Bela e saiu consagrado pela academia estadunidense. ​A grande semelhança entre os dois casos reside na deshonestidade com que Benigni higienizou a barbárie para torná-la palatável ao mercado de massas. A câmera nunca é neutra no cinema. O ato de enquadrar é, por definição, uma escolha política sobre o que revelar e o que empurrar para a invisibilidade. Quando o filme decide colocar a fome crônica, o trabalho forçado e a logística de extermínio em segundo plano para priorizar as piruetas cômicas do protagonista, essa opção estética escamoteia a verdadeira natureza da História. ​Essa abordagem se escancara em sequências absurdas, como o momento em que o protagonista toma o sistema de comunicação do campo para enviar um recado afetivo à esposa. Em um centro de extermínio real, o ato resultaria em fuzilamento sumário. Na visão cor-de-rosa do filme, os carrascos nazistas apenas dão um tapinha brincalhão na orelha do personagem e o mandam de volta ao trabalho, tratando o acontecimento como uma mera travessura. ​A escolha de encenação ganha contornos abjetos quando confrontada com a clássica crítica sobre a representação do horror. A forma de filmar, a escolha do plano e o tom de uma cena não são firulas técnicas, mas posicionamentos morais. Acontecimentos históricos fundamentados no extermínio em massa exigem ser abordados com gravidade e temor. Ao transformar a estrutura concentracional em um cenário asséptico para uma gincana familiar, a direção atua para abrandar o trauma, tornando suportável aquilo que foi intrinsecamente intolerável. Aproximações desse tipo alimentam a ilusão de que o horror do nazismo era um obstáculo simples, do qual seria possível escapar com um pouco de astúcia e otimismo. ​Vender a sobrevivência no Holocausto como o triunfo do charme individual e da dedicação paterna é uma perversidade conceitual. A Vida É Bela entrega um consolo infantilizado ao público, instrumentalizando a dor coletiva das vítimas para arrancar um choro fácil e erguer um espetáculo egocêntrico de fofura.

To quote Michael Parenti: “Saving Private Ridiculous”. Did Guido use his Jedi mind powers (something he seems to possess) on the audience? Cause there’s no way this is the same movie. Not any sort of examination from the child’s point of view, complete abandonment of the mother, all in favor of a bad vaudeville act for two hours. I’m not exaggerating. One would imagine a synopsis like this would mean the circumstances are dealt with more implicitly yet remain horrifying, but there’s not even that. It’s a cover up for refusing to engage with this tragic event in any way, popcorn over lives. Anyway, stuff that happens: -Guido harasses a woman until she loves him. -Guido delivers a speech about race superiority using his belly button. -Guido uses his mind powers and hands to make a dog move away from a hiding child. -Gudio translates German completely wrong, and not one Nazi realizes this in a camp entirely composed of Italians. Está película la vi por primera vez cuando tenía 15 años en cuarto de ESO en clase de valores (No me preguntéis porque la pusieron, a día de hoy no lo sé ni yo) y no sabía nada sobre ella. Durante el primer acto yo estaba pensando "Anda, esto es una comedia típica de los años 50 estilo Jerry Lewis", sin embargo, todo cambia cuando resulta que se trata de una película del Holocausto. Cuando termine de verla no me quede satisfecho y a día de hoy sigo sin estarlo. Voy a empezar diciendo lo bueno de esta película: Las actuaciones, sobretodo Roberto Benigni, que está formidable, y la ambientación que está muy bien realizada; y la música también está bien. Ahora voy a hablar de lo malo: La historia me pareció un despropósito, y no porque no tuviera potencial, la trama de un padre judío que intenta convencer a su hijo en un campo de concentración que están jugando un juego me parece interesante, el problema es que en vez de aprovechar dicho potencial y hacer un drama crudo sobre el Holocausto, Roberto Benigni (Que además de protagonizar la película, también la dirigió y escribió) decidió hacer una comedia bobalicona, y no es que en la primera parte la película sea una comedia y en la segunda se vuelve sería, no, incluso en el campo de concentración todavía continúan con los chascarrillos y con el pitorreo. En ningún momento la película te muestra los horrores de los campos de concentración, y teniendo en cuenta que está película salió 5 años después de "La Lista de Schindler" peor todavía. La historia gira en torno a Guido, un payasete a lo Jim Carrey que más que hacer gracia irrita, el cuál al principio de la película se enamora de una mujer llamada Dora que ya está prometida, a quien sigue de una manera que roza el acoso y lo peor de todo es que la escena en la que él le dice que quiere hacerle el amor todos los días el resto de su vida me parece realmente buena, pero yo no puedo sentir felicidad por esta pareja porque Guido en un momento dado humilla al prometido de ella, aunque fue accidental, pero luego Guido aparece con un caballo en una fiesta con invitados y Dora se va con él y de nuevo el prometido queda en ridículo y está vez frente a varias personas; qué hizo el prometido para merecer la primera y esta segunda humillación por partida doble? Absolutamente nada. Y se supone que Guido tiene que caernos bien y apoyar su relación con Dora? Lo siento, pero no cuela. Pasan los años y Guido y Dora tienen un hijo, Josué, sin embargo, por ser judíos, se llevan a Guido y a Josué, junto con el tío de Guido, a un campo de concentración, y Dora decide unirse a ellos a pesar de que no ha sido obligada a ir, y desaparece prácticamente de la película hasta el final, porque claro, para que mostrarnos su punto de vista en el campo? Mejor hacemos chistes, que es lo que uno espera en una película sobre el Holocausto. Por cierto, Guido al principio de la película tiene un amigo que desaparece de la película también, otro ejemplo de lo bien escrita que está esta obra maestra; eso por no mencionar que el tío de Guido desaparece por completo de la película también, y ahora algunos me dirá: "Murió en el campo por los nazis". Claro, obviamente, pero la película no lo muestra ni hace mención a eso, es más, Guido parece que se olvida de su tío y no le da importancia. Y hablando del campo, en una de las escenas, Guido se cuela en una sala y habla a través de los altavoces para comunicarse con Dora, y sí, muy bonita y muy cursi, pero como narices ningún soldado nazi se da cuenta? Una voz en italiano suena a través de los altavoces y a nadie le parece sospechoso, no tienen a nadie que hable en italiano que se entere de lo que suena en los altavoces, todos los soldados de ese campo son zopencos perdidos. Luego tenemos una escena en la que Josué se escapa de irse a las "duchas" (El que entiende, entiende), y se encuentra con Guido y Guido le dice que vaya a "ducharse" ya que cree que es una ducha normal, y yo me pregunto: Que se supone que tengo que sentir en esta escena? Tengo que que reírme, tengo que quedarme horrorizado? Y lo peor de todo es que al final cuando Guido muere, yo no me puedo tomar su muerte en serio, porque: Uno, lleva haciendo el payaso toda la película, y dos, este personaje se enrolló con una mujer que ya tenía pareja dejando en ridículo al prometido. Pero tranquilos, que puede empeorar aún más, cuando Josué se reúne con su madre, Dora, al final de la película, Josué está muy contento diciendo: "Hemos ganado", y Dora igual de contenta, y ninguno de ellos piensa en Guido, en si sigue vivo, ni siquiera hacen mención a él; un aplauso para esta maravilla de largometraje, y encima la película tiene las agallas de poner una narracion de Josué ya adulto diciendo de manera dramática: "Esta es la historia de lo que mi padre sacrificó y bla, bla, bla..." Hombre, pues muy triste no estabas al final gritando que habéis ganado todo contento. En fin, está película está absolutamente sobrevalorada y francamente es el equivalente a Emilia Pérez pero en Holocausto. Antes mencioné a Jerry Lewis y curiosamente el quería rodar una película llamada "The Day The Clown Cried" la cuál gira en torno al Holocausto y aunque no la terminó, estoy convencido de que habría sido mucho mejor que está película, o por lo menos habría tocado el tema con más tacto. Y quiero dejar clara una cosa: Roberto Benigni me cae bien, me parece un hombre talentoso y no creo que su intención fuera ofender, sino más bien tocar un tema serio desde una perspectiva humorística y esperanzadora en vez de triste y deprimente, pero el resultado, en mi opinión, no fue bueno. Si esta película hubiera salido en los años 50 quizás me gustaría un poco más ya que como el Holocausto fue algo reciente tendría sentido hacer este largometraje con humor para animar al público en vez de deprimirlo por lo oscura que fue este evento histórico. No sé si recomiendo esta película, la verdad es que no la disfruté en su día y la sigo sin disfrutar.

It's rare that I have hot takes. In fact, I'm not even sure if my rating for this film will even be considered a hot take. Roberto Benigni's La vita è bella ( Life is Beautiful in English) is a film that is still to this today considered one of the best films about World War II, and one of the best Italian films in (relatively) recent times. However, this is a film that just leaves me cold. Told in two parts, the first part being about the Jewish-Italian waiter Guido Orefice's (Roberto Benigni) blossoming romance with Dora (Nicoletta Braschi) in 1939, and the second part takes place in 1945, Guido and Dora are now married and have a son named Giosuè (Giorgio Cantarini) and they are all brought into concentration camps by Nazi Germany, who has occupied Northern Italy at this point in time. This is a film that definitely has its heart in the right place and a message that is good. However, that does not automatically make the film good, or even a masterpiece for that matter. Benigni wants to show us that you have to keep your head up high and find the comedy and romance in life to prevent the darkness of the world from consuming you, even in the face of the worst historical atrocity with World War II. That message is fine, but it doesn't work in this film, because any atrocity that occurs surrounding the concentration camps are pushed so far into the background that you are mostly left with Roberto Benigni's antics, and he is chewing the scenery to an obnoxious degree here. If the film was at least told through either Dora or Giosuè's point of view, Guido as a character could have worked as a shining contrast to the darkness surrounding them, kind of like how Benigni worked so wonderfully as a bright contrast to the two other protagonists of Jim Jarmusch' Down By Law . But no, everything has to be framed through Guido's point of view, and Roberto Benigni's performance is so insufferably quirky and optimistic, whilst also being incredibly one-note that it hurt my immersion into the film and the story it wanted to tell. Also, did we really need an entire first half of the film covering Guido's blossoming romance with Dora, when Dora is barely a character here? The film would have left a much bigger impact if we got to spend more time with Guido, Dora and Giosuè as a family before the concentration camps, so that the impact of Nazi Germany's presence could be felt in a more impactful manner, but no, Roberto Benigni's hunger for chewing scenery must be satisfied with that overlong, sluggishly-paced first part that serves no real purpose in the grand scheme of things. I'm just gonna stop here for my own sake. I am not a fan of this film at all, and while it does have a good message, its execution is only to the detriment of said message.

1. ¿Cómo es el ambiente moral que le tocó vivir a los personajes? Desde el primer acto en la película, se comienzan a dar indicios de como se iba infiltrando el fascismo en la sociedad italiana. Charlas casuales sobre una supuesta raza superior como si estuvieran hablando sobre el clima. La culminación de todo esto termina siendo la guerra que ya todos conocemos. Ante todo esto, Guido, el protagonista, logra envolver a su hijo en una burbuja para resguardar su inocencia en medio de todo el terror. 2. ¿Que circunstancias tuvieron que luchar los personajes? Por un lado tenemos a Guido, el padre, un hombre que la verdad, no fue de mi agrado en la primera parte de la película. Es un hombre impulsivo, impertinente e ignora las normas sociales básicas. A pesar de eso, no es una mala persona. Nunca dudo en ponerse en peligro su propia integridad en son de proteger a su hijo y esposa. Sí era fantasioso, pero no estúpido. Mi escena favorita fue el momento en el que intenta pedir ayuda al doctor, creyendo que existía alguna clase de vínculo entre ambos solo para darse cuenta que la razón por la que le dió una oportunidad de meserear no venía desde la empatía y la humanidad. Su vida y la de su familia no era lo importante, sino, el acertijo que no dejaba dormir por las noches al doctor. Guido hizo lo imposible hasta en sus últimos momentos con tal de que la experiencia traumática de experimentar un genocidio se sintiera como un campo de juegos para su hijo. Por otro lado tenemos a Dora. Ella decidió luchar por su amor y su familia durante toda la película al ignorar los ideales fascistas y clasistas de su familia para casarse y formar una familia con Guido; y más tarde en la película al ir por voluntad propia a los campos de concentración a pesar de no estar obligada, solo por no abandonar a su esposo e hijo. 3. Tipo de actitud que asumieron Guido: optimista, esperanzadora, resiliente Dora: leal, empática, resiliente Cómo historia de amor es pésima, como película histórica es mala, tampoco brilla por sus actuaciones, pero visualmente me parece muy bella y la actuación de Roberto Benigni es de las cosas más rescatables Me parece increíble como la actriz de la esposa no es capaz de emitir ninguna sola emoción, pero quizás es porque tampoco le habrán dado mucho para trabajar porque el personaje de la madre queda en tremendo segundo plano y solo sirvió para dar a luz a un niño, en fin

I really don't know how I feel about this. I'm willing to surrender myself to this story of a father trying his absolute best to fight fascism with the only tool he has available, and the emotions are predictably overpowering. Is it important to remain hopeful in even the most harrowing situations? Probably. Is there something to be said about previous generations swallowing pain so that the next can succeed? I guess. It's just not the kind of perspective that resonates with me, nor feels particularly strong when linked to one of the most pivotal atrocities in human history. The Holocaust was an unbelievably horrific act of violence. There was nothing to be hopeful of. It's a stain on history and the ramifications it produced has damned us. The lessons from this are about our cruelty, and while stories of a survival may have hope underneath them, it's not the prominent feature. I would love to believe that humans who are suffering can overcome anything through sheer hope, but that is not reality. You cannot fight ignorance with more ignorance. I try to meet films at where they're at and not where I want them to be, so this is strong in where it meets us. The second half is incredibly well done, and it's effective when it's pulling out our emotions. Unfortunately the first half is a fairly unremarkable romcom with Chaplin influences that are aggressively screaming at you. It's all tailor made for Hollywood elite sensibilities.

Creo que La vida es Bella posee méritos destacables. Hay escenas, como aquella en la que Guido le desea los buenos días a su amada, que alcanzan una notable capacidad de conmover al espectador, precisamente porque condensan una de las ideas centrales de la película: la posibilidad de encontrar belleza, afecto y sentido incluso en circunstancias profundamente adversas. En términos generales, la obra pretende construir una reflexión sobre la capacidad humana de preservar cierta luminosidad frente a la oscuridad. Mi principal objeción, y la razón por la que no considero que sea una gran película, reside en que esta premisa no termina de articularse satisfactoriamente a través de la relación entre Guido y su hijo. Me resulta particularmente problemática la decisión de construir el vínculo entre ambos sobre la base de una burbuja de mentiras destinada a ocultarle al niño la naturaleza de aquello que está ocurriendo. La invisibilización del Holocausto entra, en cierto sentido, en contradicción con la propia filosofía que la película intenta defender: encontrar belleza y esperanza dentro de la oscuridad no debería implicar necesariamente negar la existencia de esa oscuridad. Considero que la película habría, adquirido una mayor fuerza dramática y unas mayor coherencia temática si el niño hubiese sido consciente, al menos parcialmente, de la gravedad de la situación. La cuestión no radica en negar el valor de la imaginación o del juego como mecanismos de protección frente al sufrimiento, sino en que Guido termina utilizando esos recursos no tanto para ayudar a su hijo a atravesar una realidad terrible como para mantenerlo completamente al margen de ella. Si trasladamos esto a una situación cotidiana, por ejemplo, cuando un padre atraviesa dificultades económicas, lo habitual no es necesariamente construir una ficción destinada a convencer al hijo de que nada sucede. Puede intentar preservar su tranquilidad, suavizar el impacto emocional o incluso recurrir al humor para aliviar la tensión, pero eso es diferente de convertir la mentira en el mecanismo mediante el cual se niega la realidad. Por ello, considero que existe una tensión importante entre el discurso de la película y la manera en que este se materializa en Guido. Si su propuesta consiste en demostrar que incluso en las circunstancias más atroces es posible encontrar una forma de belleza o de esperanza, resulta paradójico que el procedimiento elegido para transmitir esa idea consista en ocultar precisamente aquello que hace que esa esperanza tenga significado. La luz adquiere sentido porque existe oscuridad; eliminar esta última del horizonte perceptivo del niño debilita el valor de la primera. El plano final, además, parece sugerir que el niño eventualmente comprenderá lo que realmente ocurrió y reconstruirá retrospectivamente la experiencia vivida junto a su padre. Sin embargo, precisamente por eso considero que Guido no contribuye demasiado a ese proceso de comprensión: su estrategia consiste, hasta el final, en preservar la ficción del juego. La película está bien lograda en determinados aspectos y posee momentos genuinamente conmovedores, pero considero que su tratamiento del tema central termina siendo contradictorio. La defensa de la belleza de la vida frente al horror habría resultado mucho más poderosa si la película hubiese permitido que su protagonista encontrara esa belleza sin necesidad de negar la realidad del horror.

I są w tym filmie wątki genialne, tak ten przedwojennej "przyjaźni" żydowskiego kelnera z niemieckim lekarzem i ich ponownego obozowego spotkania. Ale są też liczne irytujące potknięcia. Jak np. puszczanie przez obozowe głośniki odtwarzanej przez gramofon opery "Opowieści Hoffmanna" skomponowanej przez Jacques’a Offenbacha. Offenbach był Żydem. La Vida es Bella en el fondo dos películas de cuento. Una es una sátira del fascismo donde un payaso como Guido trata de enamorar a su princesa en medio de escenas absurdas. La otra es un intento de esconder el horror del Holocausto a un niño a través de la fantasía. Ha quedado una primera mitad icónica - como lo es su Buenos días, princesa - y una segunda mitad muy criticada y que no veo que termine de encontrar el punto. La primera mitad es muy Cabaret, hay una comedia romántica donde unos personajes que viven su vida mientras el fascismo se va imponiendo. Guido persigue a su princesa en medio de una comedia física y absurda bastante chula mientras vemos al fascismo establecido. Vemos al fascismo y sus ideas raciales ridiculizadas pero también vemos como la presión sobre los judíos va creciendo. Sin embargo, al llegar al campo de concentración, la película muta y no tiene muy claro que punto quiere tener. Transforma a Guido en un cuentacuentos, a un fabulador que a pesar del horror del que es testigo trata de esconderselo a su hijo, creando un juego. Ya la comedia absurda pierde sentido pero, ¿qué película es? ¿Una tragedia? ¿Un drama? ¿Una fábula? ¿Una comedia negra? ¿Una película de tensión y suspense? En todo esto la película termina de funcionar. No creo que su problema sea que lo trivializa, sino que no tiene claro que hacer. Quizá aún no sepamos como contar el holocausto sin más registros que el drama. Aún tiene momentos como el momento de la traducción falsa o el momento de la cena y el gratzie. Y el final del reencuentro con la madre me parece un horror, es tan edulcorado y bucólico- madre e hijo abrazándose tras bajar del tanque en el césped verde- que la película necesita que las imágenes necesiten ser matizadas por una voz de off que recuerde el sacrificio del padre. En fin, es una película que me gusta más su primera parte que la segunda. Benigni dirige y actúa bastante bien. Tiene muchos puntos positivos pero la segunda mitad, me deja muy incómodo y no considero que en el buen sentido, no sé que película veo del todo.

To make a comedy-drama film out of the Holocaust is not only an ambitious goal but a controversial one. The Holocaust is a gruesome tragedy and adding comedic elements to such a drastic event is risking the possibility of being disrespectful to Jews, holocaust survivors, and those that died during the genocide. Humor is used to present themes about child innocence and the ability, or the lack thereof, to prevent a child from finding out the true destruction of the Nazis. This approach to humor intends to invoke themes of empowerment during war and escapism as coping mechanisms  However, Roberto Benigni and Vincenzo Cerami's screenplay is oftentimes irritating to the point that it borders on distasteful in its refusal to accurately depict the Holocaust. I found it excruciatingly difficult to care about any of our characters or the repercussions of the holocaust when the world that’s lived in feels exceedingly detached from reality. One could say that this is the point of the film, and that the fable-esque storytelling is meant to convey the holocaust from the son’s perspective. I could buy into this notion if the first fifty minutes of the film were not solely comedic with brief satirical representations of Nazis. Part 1 establishes France and the World War as a surreal fantasy, which is jarring when juxtaposed to a concentration camp setting in part 2. I would not take issue with the humor if it was not as excessive or over-the-top as it was. The humor in a movie like “JoJo Rabbit” works because it’s told from a German’s child shielded perspective. The film is satirical for the majority of its runtime, and when the emotional beats occur, the themes of dictatorship, indoctrination and propaganda become horrifying to the audience. The humorous elements and failure to portray devastation in Life Is Beautiful teeter closely to an unjust telling of the holocaust. Its motifs about resilience and coping are overbearingly fantastical, hopeful and optimistic. Instead of acting as a subject matter of empowerment or coming-of-age, these themes are masquerades to hide the true horror of the holocaust. “Pan’s Labyrinth" was released in 2006 and tells the story about the Francoist regime and a child’s coping mechanism to cope under an authoritarian state. Its themes are nearly identical to those of Life Is Beautiful, communicating ideas of escapism, imagination, and child innocence as resistance. However, unlike Life Is Beautiful, Pan’s Labyrinth never shifts far enough in its tone from the tragedy surrounding our child protagonist. The film’s ending is memorably bleak, and tells the story of the Francoist regime in a respectful manner with fantastical themes remaining important but not fictitious to the point of inaccuracy. Life Is Beautiful strays too far the other direction, its emphasis of comedy and purposeful hiding about the horrors of the holocaust make it a frustrating film. Perhaps there is an inherent pessimism that is stopping myself from enjoying such an optimistic movie, and Benigni and I express a disconnect in depiction of tragedy. Its attempts to present itself visually as a 60’s technicolor-esque is admirable, but are used to further reinforce aspects of a child-like whimsical world of which I am not a fan of. A world that not only left me emotionally detached from our characters, but is ethically questionable in its presentation of the Holocaust.

Life is Beautiful is by far its most effective in the first half, when we have a Chaplin/Keaton-esque lead performance from Roberto Benigni wooing his love ("Buongiorno principessa") as the rise of fascism in Italy grows. The key, the eggs, the hat, the silks; all laying the groundwork for the love story to come - and here, Life is Beautiful. You do see fascism rising in Italy, but the ideology is ridiculed in really funny ways that speak to the absurdity of a 'superior race' (how could you not be superior with those earlobes and belly buttons?!). It's heart-warming, charming, and laugh-out-loud funny, yet still incisive, and this is where the movie thrives. And then we get a time jump and we lose our way a little bit. We still get Guido's usual sense of humour, but it becomes only for the benefit of Giosue as opposed to any broader critique. We get to see a very sanitized version of concentration camps (there's really only one shot of bodies, obscured by a thick fog/smoke), and the movie shies away from showing anything truly horrifying on screen, instead choosing to do it all off-camera or between scenes. The movie thus puts you in the same place as Giosue and hides the truth - but we're not a 4 year old child! By doing so it diminishes the suffering that Jews and other marginalized groups went through, and presents radical optimism as the only way through unspeakable tragedy. The Nazis were a ruthless, hate-filled, unrelenting methodical machine hellbent on extermination, and the way they're shown in the second half of the film is as if they are simply incompetent - a key example of this is the translation scene when they first arrive, and choosing not to subtitle the German officers instructions; the scene actually wouldn't change that much, but we as the audience would be more exposed to the reality, whereas Giosue stays in the metaphorical dark. In fact, rather than anything actually depicted on screen, the most heartbreaking scene is when the Doctor pulls Guido aside and asks him a riddle. It's the extermination of hope that really hits & propels the movie towards it's inevitable conclusion. And somehow Benigni wins best actor this year (in the same year as Tom Hanks for Saving Private Ryan , Ed Norton in American History X , Jeff Bridges in Big Lebowski , and Jim Carrey in both Eternal Sunshine and Truman Show ). Will never understand this decision - although he is genuinely fantastic at all the comedic elements and carries the movie through those, he is severely out of his depth when the movie tries to get more serious (and maybe partly why it doesn't in places). What we end up with is an incredible first half with a second half that feels very out of place. My biggest pet peeve in watching movies is when something could be great but isn't. I see why it's loved but the lack of realism hurts it a lot (and still could've worked!). A real shame because I was looking forward to this rewatch a lot - I remember loving this as a kid and thinking it was such an important movie for education about the Holocaust & concentration camps, but having learnt a lot more in the intervening years it really falls short. Still a good movie but certainly has lost a lot of shine over the years. 7.5/10

What begins as this whimsical, almost slapstick romantic comedy transforms so swiftly into something profoundly devastating that the tonal shift is almost a shock to the system. Somehow, the film manages to preserve that same sense of wonder throughout, even as the circumstances become increasingly horrific. There’s something so deeply moving about Guido’s determination to preserve his son’s innocence in the face of unimaginable cruelty. The lengths he goes to protect him from the reality of their circumstances, transforming the horrors of a concentration camp into an elaborate game, are as heartbreaking as they are extraordinary. What I find particularly affecting is how the humor never really disappears; it simply takes on an entirely different meaning. What initially serves as a source of joy becomes an act of resistance, a means of survival, and ultimately an extraordinary expression of love and selflessness. And that final wink. Quite possibly the saddest wink in any film, truly. Is the film flawed? Absolutely. Its sentimentality can feel excessive, and its treatment of such horrific subject matter is not without its complications. But ultimately, it’s such a lovely reminder of the importance of finding beauty in even the darkest of circumstances, not because that beauty diminishes the horror, but because our capacity for love, laughter, and imagination can endure in spite of it. A beautiful and heartbreaking testament to a father’s love. 8.5/10

Every single time it kept going I laughed harder and harder. There’s something genuinely special about a movie that can have you laughing one minute and absolutely destroy you the next. Those type of movies are always held in quite high esteem for me (Everything Everywhere All At Once comes to mind, although this isn't better than that or something like the end of Click, although this is much better than that) and there is just something about mixing laughter/crying and happiness/sadness into one. They are both emotions and actions that are so closely tied together that when you consume something that envokes both at the same time it sends this pushing and pulling signal to the brain that, for me at least, just breaks me down almost every time. This manages to balance those two things so effortlessly, which is what makes it such a beautiful and heartbreaking experience. Roberto Benigni take a fucking bow. Im writing this review immediately after watching so I haven't looked it up but did this man receive all the awards? Him finding little moments of happiness in a situation where there should be none was so bittersweet. All I could do was sit there and say "what a good Dad" out loud. Like what more is there to say. Roberto Benigni was making me proper crack up at so many points in this movie from the start all the way to the finish. I loved how they didn't show anything that actually happened to anyone until that one scene of the bodies piled up. That only happened when Giosué was sleeping as well. Almost as if it was shown the only time that Guido didn't need to put up the act in front of his son. Brilliant visual storytelling. É difícil explicar o tamanho do sentimento que esse filme desperta. É sobre amor em sua forma mais pura, sobre encontrar beleza mesmo quando o mundo parece ter perdido completamente a sua. O que mais me emociona é pensar que, às vezes, amar alguém é tentar preservar a beleza do mundo para essa pessoa, mesmo quando você já não consegue enxergá-la. É fazer do impossível um lugar menos assustador. É escolher o amor tantas vezes que ele acaba se tornando maior do que qualquer circunstância. E talvez seja por isso que esse filme seja tão especial para mim. Porque ele me lembra que a vida pode ser injusta, dolorosa e imprevisível, mas ainda assim existem motivos para sorrir, pessoas pelas quais vale a pena tudo e momentos que tornam a existência extraordinária. No fim, A Vida é Bela não me faz acreditar que tudo sempre ficará bem. Ele me faz acreditar que, mesmo quando as coisas não estão bem, o amor ainda pode ser a coisa mais bonita que existe. meu filme favorito, meu coração em forma de cinema. 5 estrelas nunca serão suficientes. ⭐️
